_metadata.interpretation: Subjectively elicited, time-invariant district priors conditional on structural-driver assumptions. Numerical centres and concentrations are analyst assumptions, not parameter estimates from the cited sources. Fine district differences are not measured effects.

units.p: Monthly exit probability, all exit mechanisms combined.
units.gamma: Expected new episodes per month divided by the under-5 population; fraction, not percent.
units.omega: Total standard deviation of monthly new episodes divided by the under-5 population; fraction, not percent and not excess variability.

elicitation.parameterization: For elicited mean m and concentration kappa, a=m*kappa and b=(1-m)*kappa; variance=m*(1-m)/(kappa+1).
elicitation.informativeness: High conditional informativeness is imposed as requested; the contextual literature does not independently justify this precision or identify absolute incidence, duration or process variability. Concentration is not a literal number of observed children or months. Sparse contextual evidence widens all priors, including omega, without raising its mean.
elicitation.absolute_scale: Elicited monthly means span p=0.17-0.34, gamma=0.0035-0.0090 and omega=0.0015-0.0050. These scales were selected directly, without using nutritional prevalence, prevalence rankings or prevalence-based back-calculation.
elicitation.district_aggregation: Judgmental district mixtures of rural livelihood zones, towns and documented displacement settings; exact under-5 mixture weights were unavailable.
elicitation.exit_assumption: Differences in p primarily represent hypothesized recovery-access differences, conditional on otherwise comparable natural episode dynamics. No district-specific fatality or spontaneous-recovery evidence was established, so no mortality-based upward adjustment was made. Acute-and-fatal versus chronic-and-persistent episode patterns remain unclassified.
elicitation.omega_assumption: Centres represent recurring food, disease-exposure, climate, livelihood and movement processes. Persistent isolation affects recovery and food access but does not by itself imply volatile arrivals. No survey-related property determines omega.
elicitation.dependence: Separate marginal Beta distributions are supplied; cross-parameter and cross-district dependence is unspecified.
elicitation.validation_scope: JSON schema, district coverage, positivity, units and Beta moments checked. Numerical centres have not been clinically validated. Prior predictive and concentration-sensitivity checks are needed when population sizes and the likelihood data are available.

research_limitations: The FSNAU tools landing page was inaccessible. The accessible 2016 joint FSNAU-FEWS NET livelihood profiles, baseline archive and 2015 joint livelihood map supplied structural alternatives.
The FEWS NET Somalia landing page and direct 2015 livelihood-map page returned HTTP 403. The same joint livelihood products hosted by FSNAU were used instead.

FSNAU publications were accessible, but several 2017-2019 climate downloads and individual baseline links failed. Accessible October 2020 and January 2021 climate updates, the October 2020 market update and older structural profiles were used. A complete 2017-2021 contextual sequence was not recovered; peak events were not used to set time-invariant centres.

Mixed post-seasonal technical releases and nutrition-survey reports were excluded because reliable outcome-free extraction was not assured. No district-specific typical IPC Acute Food Insecurity phase was verified across 2017-2021, and none was invented or used as a numeric calibration input.

The SARA archive description was accessible, but its report download failed and the health-ministry PDF required verification. Separable health-system sections of the World Bank 2021 report reproduced WHO SARA regional infrastructure and staffing evidence instead. District-level facility density, longitudinal CMAM coverage, supply reliability and episode fatality were not established; service-access differences are explicit contextual inferences.

The OCHA Somalia landing page returned HTTP 403. OCHA 2020 Humanitarian Access Overview was read through an accessible mirror; district political and road-access context was supplemented by EASO September 2021. These are partial-period evidence and do not establish an invariant access classification for every district.

Several IOM DTM document opens failed or returned HTTP 403. UNHCR-hosted CCCM material, the Afgooye site assessment, a UNDP 2020 displacement account and a UNHCR 2018 Galkayo account supplied alternatives. IOM 2019 movement-report search extracts were corroborative only. Missing district hosting evidence was not treated as proof of no displacement.

An attempted open of the OCHA December 2018 mixed bulletin unexpectedly exposed prohibited outcome text. That text was discarded, the entire bulletin was excluded from elicitation evidence, and no displayed outcome quantity or description informed the priors. Strict absence of incidental exposure therefore cannot be certified.
Events and programme changes after 2021 were not used to characterize 2017-2021 conditions. Later-hosted copies of older reports were used only for their historical content.

evidence_routing.meaning: Sources establish contextual mechanisms; every numerical mapping from context to p, gamma or omega is an elicitation assumption, not a reported source estimate.
